usage_description: Irrigation pump on a separately metered controlled load circuit
annual_cost_estimate_aud: ~$190-$304 per hectare per year (500-800 kWh/ha at 20c/kWh)
notes: MOST RELEVANT FOR RIVERLAND IRRIGATORS. Irrigation pumps qualify as controlled load appliances under SA tariff rules. Pump runs overnight at ~50% of standard rate. Requires a second meter installed. Directly supports the MVP Water & Irrigation scheduling module — scheduling pumps to overnight saves ~$20/kWh compared to peak daytime use.
source_document: EnergyAustralia Controlled Load Tariff Information + SA Power Networks Pricing Proposal 2025-26
data_verified: Yes — EnergyAustralia explicitly lists irrigation pumps as controlled load appliances

usage_description: Farm with rooftop or ground-mounted solar (export to grid)
annual_cost_estimate_aud: Reduces import bill — value depends on self-consumption rate
notes: From 1 July 2025 retailers set their own feed-in rates — these cannot be below zero. ESCOSA reports SA feed-in rates ranged from 0-6c/kWh at 30 June 2025. Solar self-consumption (avoiding import) is worth 30-40c/kWh. Riverland farms with high daytime electricity use (cooling, processing) benefit most from solar self-consumption.
source_document: Energy Retail Price Offers Comparison Report 2024-25
